seed_policy: One independent stream per setting and run, from numpy SeedSequence([20240601, setting_index, run_index]); the base seed is stated in the paper. Settings are not paired.
failure_policy: A trial where curve_fit raises, does not converge, or returns k_hat<=0 or non-finite k or variance at any temperature is excluded from the statistics, counted per setting, and listed in the output; the failure fraction is reported, coverage is stated as conditional on success, and a bound counting failures as misses is also reported.
ci_method: Wilson binomial interval for coverage; bootstrap (1000 resamples) or analytic standard error for bias, SD and correlation (Fisher z).
acceptance: Coverage of the t interval for Ea and ln A lies within the 95% Wilson interval of 0.95 in at least 90% of the cell-parameter checks with sigma<=0.02 and n_points>=12, with no trend in pass rate across sigma or n_points; any single failure is reported.
Observed SD/theoretical SE is within 1±0.1 in those cells.
Bias of Ea_hat is below 2 SE_MC (or below 10% of the SD) in those cells.
Noise-free oracles recover Ea and lnA to the stated tolerance.
Low-noise SD/SE limiting-case oracle is within 0.1 of 1.

precision.reason: Distinguishing coverage 0.95 from the 0.90 typical of the failing regime needs a half-width of about 0.03 or less; 400 runs give about 0.021.

oracles.name: noise_free_Ea
oracles.check: With sigma=0 the pipeline must recover Ea exactly (unit weights are used because the NLS variance is zero); this checks the code only, not the statistics.
oracles.reference: derivation: with sigma=0, c=exp(-k t) exactly, NLS (curve_fit ftol=xtol=1e-10) returns k to solver tolerance, ln k = lnA - Ea/(R T) is exactly linear in 1/T, so the slope is -Ea/R and Ea_hat=50000 J/mol.

oracles.name: noise_free_lnA
oracles.check: With sigma=0 the pipeline must recover ln A exactly, which checks the centring back-transformation; the 1e-6 tolerance is at least 100 times the curve_fit solver error (ftol=xtol=1e-10).
oracles.reference: derivation: the intercept at the centred 1/T is lnA-(Ea/R)*xbar, and adding back the slope times xbar returns lnA=16.

oracles.name: sampling_window_kt_max
oracles.check: At every one of the five temperatures the sampling grid ends at max(t)=3/k, so the worst violation of max(t)*k=3 is 0; this catches a wrong sampling window that noise-free recovery cannot see.
oracles.reference: derivation: t=linspace(0,3/k,n) has max(t)=3/k, so max(t)*k - 3 = 0 at each temperature and the worst violation = 0.
oracles.measure: max over the five temperatures of |max(t)*k - 3|

oracles.name: low_noise_SD_over_theory_SE
oracles.check: At very low noise (sigma in units of c0) and 40 points the linearisation is accurate, so the observed SD of Ea_hat over 500 runs equals the closed-form linearised SE computed with the pipeline's own weights 1/var(ln k) (ratio 1); this exercises the real weighted pipeline and the theory code.
oracles.reference: derivation: for small sigma the NLS estimator is asymptotically normal with Var(k_hat) = sigma^2/sum(t_i^2 exp(-2 k t_i)), and the weighted regression is linear in ln k, so Var(Ea_hat) = R^2 [(X'WX)^-1]_11 with W=diag(1/var(ln k)) and SD/SE = 1; with 500 runs the relative error of the SD is 1/sqrt(2*500) = 0.032, so 0.1 is about 3 sigma.

oracles.name: low_noise_coverage_95
oracles.check: At low noise and 40 points the nominal 95% interval for Ea (S3) should contain the true Ea in about 95% of repeated runs.
oracles.reference: derivation: for small sigma the weighted regression estimator is approximately normal with the reported SE, so coverage of the nominal 95% interval = 0.95; the binomial SE with 500 runs is sqrt(0.95*0.05/500) = 0.0097, so 0.04 is about 4 sigma.

oracles.name: low_noise_reportedSE_over_SD
oracles.check: The mean reported SE of Ea_hat from the regression should equal the observed SD of Ea_hat over runs, which tests the weights and covariance that feed the interval.
oracles.reference: derivation: with correct weights 1/var(ln k) the regression covariance (X'WX)^-1 = the true variance of the estimator, so mean reported SE / observed SD = 1; with 500 runs the SD has relative error 1/sqrt(2*500) = 0.032, so 0.1 is about 3 sigma.

criteria.name: noiseless_lnA_error
criteria.what: The noise-free pipeline recovers ln A.

simplifications.replaces: fit k with c0 unspecified (c0 may be free)
simplifications.because: c0 is known and fixed to 1 so each temperature fit has one parameter
simplifications.effect: Uncertainty in k is smaller than with a free c0, and the small-sample nonlinear bias of the NLS fit is reduced.
simplifications.probe: Rerun one cell with c0 free and compare the SD of Ea_hat.

simplifications.replaces: a standard definition of bias, spread and coverage cited from a source
simplifications.because: none of the retrieved sources states these definitions word for word
simplifications.effect: None on numbers; definitions are the usual ones (bias=mean(hat)-true, spread=SD of hat, coverage=fraction of intervals containing truth).
simplifications.probe: The definitions are stated explicitly in the paper.

simplifications.replaces: exact (non-linearised) error propagation as the theory for the spread of the estimates
simplifications.because: the linearised theory ignores that stage-two weights are estimated from stage-one data, which is the source of any small-sample coverage failure
simplifications.effect: The theory SE may understate the observed SD at high noise.

simplifications.replaces: temperature: the exact temperatures are not given by the topic, only a 10-fold range of k
simplifications.because: the topic fixes only a 10-fold range of k, so five temperatures are chosen equally spaced in 1/T starting at 320 K (about 285 K at the other end)
simplifications.effect: A wider or narrower 1/T range would scale the Ea SE inversely with the range.
simplifications.probe: State the temperatures and the 1/T range in the paper.

simplifications.replaces: all simulated runs entering the statistics, including coverage of the 95% interval
simplifications.because: runs with a failed fit or k_hat<=0 at any temperature cannot be log-transformed and are excluded
simplifications.effect: Coverage, bias and spread at high noise and few points are conditional on success and may look better than the unconditional estimator.
simplifications.probe: Report the failure fraction per cell and the coverage bound counting failures as misses.

simplifications.replaces: a continuous range of noise levels and of numbers of time points
simplifications.because: noise level and number of time points are varied on a finite grid (5 sigma values x 5 n_points values), with sigma in units of c0
simplifications.effect: Behaviour between grid values and outside 0.005 to 0.1 or 5 to 40 points is interpolated or unknown.
simplifications.probe: Check that SD varies smoothly with sigma and n_points across the grid.

simplifications.replaces: general sampling times, with the sampling window set by the topic as 0 to 3/k at each temperature
simplifications.because: times are equally spaced, t=linspace(0,3/k,n_points), using the true k at each temperature
simplifications.effect: An analyst without the true k would choose a different window; the SD of k_hat and of Ea_hat depends on the window.
simplifications.probe: State the window and its dependence on true k in the paper; the deterministic check max(t)*k=3 verifies it.

simplifications.replaces: the full distribution of the estimates by summary statistics of spread (SD, IQR-based spread, RMSE)
simplifications.because: heavy tails at high noise make the SD alone unrepresentative
simplifications.effect: SD may be dominated by a few runs, while the IQR-based spread understates tail risk.
simplifications.probe: Report median bias and IQR beside mean and SD and the number of runs beyond 5 SE.

simplifications.replaces: the per-temperature k fits being summarised individually
simplifications.because: the k_hat estimates are reported as a per-temperature bias table, not as a figure
simplifications.effect: Stage-one bias of k_hat is visible only in a table and could be overlooked.
simplifications.probe: Inspect the per-temperature k_hat bias table for bias in ln k_hat that grows with sigma.

simplifications.replaces: the activation energy being estimated from independent data
simplifications.because: Ea and ln A come from one weighted regression, so their estimates are strongly correlated, with the 1/T centre about 3.3e-3 K^-1 from zero
simplifications.effect: Marginal intervals for Ea and ln A do not describe the joint uncertainty; coverage of the pair is not 0.95 for rectangular regions.
simplifications.probe: Report corr(Ea_hat, ln A_hat) and the theoretical covariance ellipse in the scatter figure.

simplifications.replaces: coverage of the true value by the 95 percent interval over all runs, for each parameter
simplifications.because: coverage is computed only over runs with a successful fit and from a single interval construction (t quantile with 3 df, residual-scaled covariance), with a normal-quantile interval as a secondary
simplifications.effect: Reported coverage may be higher than the unconditional coverage at high noise and few points, and depends on the interval construction.
simplifications.probe: Report the failure fraction per cell and the coverage bound counting failures as misses, and compare the t and normal intervals.

simplifications.replaces: the decay coefficient k at each temperature being reported as a headline result with its own bias, spread and coverage
simplifications.because: k_hat per temperature is an intermediate stage; its bias is only tabulated per temperature and its uncertainty is used as the stage-two weight
simplifications.effect: Stage-one bias or non-normality of k_hat is not shown in a figure and could be overlooked.
simplifications.probe: Inspect the per-temperature k_hat bias table with its Monte Carlo standard error across sigma and n_points.

simplifications.replaces: the activation energy Ea being recovered with both A and the temperature scale unknown, or with a free c0
simplifications.because: A and Ea are the truth values of the simulation (ln A=16, Ea=50 kJ/mol), c0 and T are known exactly, and only one true Ea is studied
simplifications.effect: Bias, spread and coverage of Ea_hat are shown for one parameter set and one 1/T range and may not carry over to other Ea or temperature ranges.
simplifications.probe: State the single parameter set in the paper; optionally rerun one cell with a different Ea and compare SD/SE_theory.

simplifications.replaces: the correlation between the Ea and ln A estimates being described by a full joint analysis
simplifications.because: it is summarised by the Pearson correlation over runs and a theoretical 95% covariance ellipse in one scatter figure at a single setting
simplifications.effect: The correlation is shown for the chosen setting only, and a Pearson coefficient does not describe heavy tails at high noise.
simplifications.probe: Compare the observed correlation with the theoretical correlation from the weighted regression covariance across the grid.

model.summary: First-order decay c=c0 exp(-kt) with Temperature-law k(T), additive Gaussian noise, NLS fit of k per temperature, then weighted linear regression of ln k on centred 1/T.
assumptions: iid Gaussian noise with constant SD
model.holds_for: sigma from 0.005 to 0.1 of c0, 5 to 40 points per temperature, k t_max=3.

equations.derivation: Integrating dc/dt = -k c with c(0)=c0 gives c = c0 exp(-kt).
Temperature law as given in the topic statement.

equations.formula: ln k = ln A - Ea / (R * T)
equations.derivation: Take the natural log of E2; regressing ln k on 1/T has slope -Ea/R and intercept ln A.

steps.name: NLS fit of k
steps.does: Fits k to one temperature's noisy c(t) with c0 fixed, returning k_hat and var(k_hat).
relations: noise-free data returns k_hat equal to k to solver tolerance

steps.name: Weighted Temperature-law regression
steps.does: Weighted least squares of ln k_hat on 1/T minus its mean, weights 1/var(ln k), then back-transforms to Ea and lnA with covariance.
relations: the Ea-lnA covariance is positive because the centre of 1/T is positive

steps.name: 95% interval
steps.does: Forms Ea_hat ± q SE with q the t(3 df) quantile (SE scaled by residual reduced chi-square) or the normal quantile (nominal weights), and checks whether the truth is inside.
